title: Inventorying dependencies
purpose: `deps scan` lists every package the workspace's npm, NuGet and Maven/Gradle manifests and lockfiles declare, with its version, the file it came from, and whether it's direct or transitive, production or dev. That inventory is what the vulnerability and licence commands read, one source per command, so you choose which service sees your dependency list. `deps diff` lists what was added, removed, upgraded or downgraded between two git refs.
inputs: The workspace, which must be inside a git repository, with `--ecosystem`, `--include-transitive` and `--include-dev` to narrow or widen it. `deps diff` takes `--from` a commit, tag or branch, and `--to` another, or the working tree when it's left out.
examples: toil util deps scan --include-transitive | toil osv vulns
verifies: No check of its own beyond reading every file it lists: a manifest that exists but can't be read is reported as `DEPS_FILE_SKIPPED`.
limits: A lockfile wins over its manifest. In an npm v7+ lockfile, hoisted packages count as direct, and Yarn 2+ lockfiles give no packages. `deps diff` runs git and fails with `GIT_NOT_FOUND` without it, and a ref git can't read gives an empty inventory for that side, so check a ref you've typed by hand.
